entries.subject: Celestia native nucleus illustration and catalog scale
entries.finding: Superseded 2026-09-16: the Celestia generic mesh was a shared illustration with no relation to this nucleus, and its catalogue radius was an estimate. The package now shows a smooth ellipsoid at the published effective radius (Boehnhardt et al. (1999), A&A 341, 912); no mesh from Celestia is retained.
entries.revisitWhen: A measured shape model of this nucleus (radar, spacecraft or a convex lightcurve inversion with a stated pole) would replace the ellipsoid.

entries.subject: Published event and observation context
entries.finding: Retained intake decision: Grigg–Skjellerup was Giotto’s second comet encounter. The spacecraft passed about 200 km from its nucleus in July 1992, six years after visiting Halley. The cited material supplies explanatory context; it does not qualify photographic terrain on this nucleus.

entries.subject: Published effective nucleus radius
entries.finding: Boehnhardt et al. (1999), A&A 341, 912: effective radius 1.5 km. The nucleus is elongated, with a body axis ratio of 0.9 or less; the minimum elongation is displayed. Used as the volume-equivalent radius of the displayed ellipsoid.
